### B-008

**Tabgha dashboard says CONNECTION LOST while a relayed request is running**

| Signal | Priority | Status | Effort |
|:---:|---|---|---|
| 🟠 | 🔶 P2 | Investigate | 🟢 Small |

💻 **→ Human action required: No**<br />Next: reproduce and identify the original timeout using the new endpoint and IPC-method diagnostics.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Owner test on Tabgha 2026-11-05: during a request relayed to Neo Tokyo-3 (about 80 s), Tabgha's dashboard showed *LIVE · CONNECTION LOST — Request timed out; outcome may be unknown.. Run npm start -- open dashboard again if the service restarted.* The service had been up two minutes and the reply arrived. The message is the scheduler/brain call timeout reaching the browser; one failed poll is shown as a lost connection, with a doubled full stop and a misleading restart hint. |
| **Reproduce** | On a base that is not the main one, ask something in its dashboard chat while the main base takes over a minute to answer. |
| **Check** | A slow or failed poll is retried before anything is shown; a real loss says what is unreachable; the call that timed out is found and fixed or given a fitting limit; no doubled punctuation; a test covers a poll that fails once. |

<details>
<summary>Next action, estimates and evidence</summary>

**Next action / closure evidence:** Partial fix in [PR #153](https://github.com/voidbrain/nerv/pull/153), 2026-11-06: one failed poll preserves the last view and retries on the regular interval; repeated failures probe authenticated status and distinguish REFRESH DELAYED, STATUS UNAVAILABLE (HTTP error) and SERVICE UNREACHABLE (no reply). A successful poll clears the warning. GET reads have a 10 s bound; writes are neither retried nor given the read timeout. API errors name method/path, IPC timeouts name process/method/limit, and the banner removes doubled punctuation and the unsupported restart hint. Regression covers transient failures, recovery, status reachability, session expiry, read bounds, no write replay, and dashboard REST reads during a pending relay. The old report lacks endpoint/method details; the original timeout cause remains unverified, so B-008 stays Investigate until reproduced and fixed or given an evidenced fitting limit.

**Estimates:** Small remaining effort. Reassessed 2026-11-06: misleading connection warning and missing diagnostics repaired; original timeout investigation remains. Reassessed again after #153 CI: Small remains valid; no new evidence identifies the original call.

### B-021

**A question from Misato closes the sortie, and the answer opens a new one**

| Signal | Priority | Status | Effort |
|:---:|---|---|---|
| 🟡 | 🔺 P1 | Implemented | 🟢 Small |

💻 **→ Human action required: No**<br />Next: correct the recorded real-model topic-change failure and reconcile forwarded-answer timeouts.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Owner report 2026-11-05 (S-E16D, S-7B04): Misato asked *Which specific file in ~/NERV-files would you like me to read?* and the sortie closed with Debrief: done; the answer *shopping.txt* became a new sortie, and the consultant advised on it from scratch. Misato's plan has only two shapes, an action or a final reply, so a question is recorded as the final reply. |
| **Reproduce** | Ask Misato something she must ask back about (*read a file in ~/NERV-files*), then answer. |
| **Check** | A question keeps the sortie open, waiting for the owner (Debrief not lit, shown like an approval wait); the next message in the same conversation continues that sortie; a short answer (up to 8 words) goes straight to Misato, a longer one gets the consultant again as a follow-up with its first advice in view (it may say none); an unanswered question closes the sortie after 24 hours as no answer; a restart does not close a sortie waiting for an answer as interrupted. Owner addition 2026-11-06: a clearly unrelated message cancels the wait and starts a new sortie; length alone never decides. |

<details>
<summary>Next action, estimates and evidence</summary>

**Next action / closure evidence:** Reassessed 2026-11-07 at owner request: dashboard/control-flow acceptance is agent-executable; it does not require an owner to drive the browser. Browser waiting-state acceptance now passes; frozen real-model evidence confirms a topic-change failure (final reply instead of newRequest). Backend/Telegram/signed-link correctness stays distinct from that competence finding. See [evaluation assessment](decisions/evaluation-and-improvement.md). The previous owner script is a reusable agent scenario, not an owner-only prerequisite. Actual Telegram device evidence is only needed for claims about phone display/receipt. Known forwarded-answer timeout remains unresolved; no verification is inferred from changing the actor.  Implemented 2026-11-06 on `fix/misato-clarification`. Misato has a third plan shape `{"ask": …}`: the ledger records `misato.asked` (conversation, 24-hour expiry), the next message in that conversation is claimed once as `misato.answered` and continues the same sortie; up to 8 words go straight to Misato, longer answers get the consultant again with `previousAdvice`. A clear topic change makes Misato return `{"newRequest": true}` on the first turn of the answer: the old sortie is speared (nothing ran in it for the new request) and a fresh sortie answers. Questions survive restart (`resumable`/`interrupted` skip them), expire once as `misato.unanswered` (sortie failed, one reply saying nothing was resumed), and are bound to their conversation (a Telegram message cannot answer a dashboard question; messages in one conversation are serialised). An approval resume after a clarification keeps the original request and does not consult again. Forwarded questions: the sortie stays open on this base; the answer goes to the main base in the same conversation; if the main base is unavailable or changed, the answer stays waiting and is never run locally. Dashboard: a pending question shows as waiting at Misato's apartment, Debrief unlit; Comms shows the question, the answer and an expiry. Known limit: if a forwarded answer times out after the main base already took it, this base keeps waiting while the main base has moved on; the next message is then forwarded as an answer. **Scenario script (dashboard browser/agent; Bot protocol and optional phone checks separately):** (1) `Read a file in ~/NERV-files` → Misato asks which file; the dashboard shows the sortie waiting, Debrief unlit. (2) `shopping.txt` → same sortie continues (same S- id in the dashboard), no second sortie. (3) Repeat (1), then `What is on my calendar tomorrow?` → the first sortie is shown as stood down, a new sortie answers. (4) Repeat (1), restart the service (`nerv service restart`, or stop and run `nerv serve`), then answer → still the same sortie.

**Estimates:** Small remaining. Reassessed 2026-11-08: browser and real-model evidence recorded; fix the confirmed model topic-change failure and forwarded-answer timeout before closure. Historical estimate: owner check on a real base. Reassessed 2026-11-06 after implementation and automated checks.

### B-043

**Process queue saturation during Windows cross-base execution test**

| Signal | Priority | Status | Effort |
|:---:|---|---|---|
| 🟠 | 🔺 P1 | Investigate | 🟡 Medium |

💻 **→ Human action required: No**<br />Reproduce queue saturation and identify which background RPC producers overlap.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | PR #198 Windows run 42401648023 failed in the existing cross-base kaji.run test: ProcessClient.call rejected Runtime.loop's finish RPC with “Process queue is full” (-32004). The other Windows run on the same candidate passed. No CRT code runs in that backend path; the exact cause remains unverified. |
| **Reproduce** | Run test/kaji-run.test.ts with slow child replies or constrained scheduling and trace pending/waiting RPCs; the fixture starts 200 ms heartbeats and a 100 ms resumer. Overlapping periodic work is a hypothesis, not an established cause. |
| **Check** | A deterministic regression explains the observed saturation. Background work stays bounded; preserve the process queue safeguard. The cross-base path records a terminal result or an explicit failure without lost/duplicate remote effects. Windows and full-suite checks pass; do not merely widen a timeout/queue or weaken assertions. |

<details>
<summary>Next action, estimates and evidence</summary>

**Next action / closure evidence:** Investigate with a controlled slow-child fixture and per-producer request counts. Keep this finding open even if a diagnostic CI retry passes. CRT retuning does not claim to fix this backend/test reliability issue. Review source tick overlap and saturation handling before choosing the owning fix.

**Estimates:** Medium remaining effort, provisionally 2–3 focused days including deterministic reproduction, fix, integration and Windows verification. Estimated 2026-11-07; root cause is uncertain and the estimate must be reassessed after reproduction.

### F-012

**Resume a specific paused job after its provider limit resets**

| Signal | Priority | Status | Effort |
|:---:|---|---|---|
| 🔴 | 🔺 P1 | Open | 🔴 Large |

💻 **→ Human action required: No**<br />Define durable waiting jobs and implement an authorized browser/editor adapter that rechecks the exact job before resuming once.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | User wants NERV Agency to resume a web-chat job or Claude Code job in VS Code after a three-hour token-limit pause. This capability is not implemented. |
| **Reproduce** | Ask to resume an identified job after its reported reset time; keep its worker awake and session available. |
| **Check** | Persist target, permission, reset time, expiry and attempts; verify readiness and unchanged job identity; resume once; notify outcome; survive restart; handle longer limits, logout, closed tabs, sleeping workers, changed tasks and already-resumed jobs without duplicate actions. |

<details>
<summary>Next action, estimates and evidence</summary>

**Next action / closure evidence:** Prefer supported application commands/APIs. Use a browser worker or narrowly scoped desktop automation only when required. Adapter capability and host permission must be observed, not inferred. At the deadline inspect actual availability: three hours passing is not proof of a reset. Persist a bounded retry/expiry policy, cancellation, execution lease and result reconciliation. Recheck account/session/window/job identity after sleep or restart; do not replay stale clicks. Permission covers resuming the named job only, not accepting unrelated tool/security prompts or bypassing provider limits. Never place a model-originated resume instruction above user policy. The coordinator can schedule on an always-on host, but execution waits for the target worker and authenticated session. CLI/headless coding adapters should expose resumable job IDs where available; VS Code integration is not assumed to provide such an API. Required evaluations include changed button/DOM, an expired session, revised target content, already-running state and an uncertain click acknowledgement. Depends on F-003 durable scheduling and F-005/F-006 execution capabilities.

**Estimates:** Large remaining effort. Estimated 2026-11-01; adapter feasibility and real host acceptance remain unverified. Reassessed 2026-11-07: explicit prerequisite outcomes preserve the existing scope and remaining-work estimate; independent slices can proceed.

### F-045

**Pilots: a roster of permanent agents that grows, specialises and is chosen per request**

| Signal | Priority | Status | Effort |
|:---:|---|---|---|
| 🔴 | 🔶 P2 | Open | 🔴 Large |

💻 **→ Human action required: No**<br />Next: pilots offered by other bases over the Kaji line; other-provider/cloud pilot routing remains planned.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Issue** | Owner questions 2026-11-05: NERV needs permanent agents (a coder, the 3D expert on Tabgha, and others as jobs require: a Photoshop expert), a generic one for anything else, specialists that grow from it, and automatic choice. The design already names pilots (F-025: pilots run in the EVA class of their stage, watermelon trust) but has no roster. Consultants (F-041) become pilots asked only for advice (owner, 2026-11-05). |
| **Reproduce** | Ask Aoba for an image edit or a coding job: there is no pilot to give it to. |
| **Check** | **Definition as data:** a pilot is a role and domain (topics, keywords), skills, tools, a model, a memory scope, an EVA class and a trust stage (Prototype, Test, Production), with its parent; most share the base's model, a separate model only when its evaluations justify it. **Roster:** a registry like the Kaji one; each base offers its pilots in the heartbeat; the owner adds, renames, retires and pins. **Generic pilot:** one per base, takes any job no specialist covers, in the most restrictive EVA its stage allows. **Two ways of use:** asked for advice (the F-041 consultant rules: at most one per topic by default, the owner's pin, then the main base's own, then the best record, the next as fallback, "ask both" per topic; advice is data, never a vote or an action) or put in charge of the job (acts in its EVA, effects by card). **Choice:** Misato routes by domain and keywords, base, stage allowed for the action and record; unclear goes to the generic pilot or a question; the card shows the pilot, its stage and base, and the owner can change it; routing accuracy is measured. **New specialists found automatically:** unmatched domains, tools the generic pilot lacked and repeated failures are counted per domain; past a threshold (e.g. three unmatched in 30 days, or one missing tool) NERV proposes a pilot (or an extension of an existing one) on a card with the sorties behind it, its skills, tools and installs; created at Prototype. **Split and merge by evidence:** a split when sorties cluster in a subdomain and a narrower set scores better; a merge when two overlap and neither is better; lineage kept. **Learning (owner decision 2026-11-05: the recommendation):** new evaluation cases from failures are added automatically and shown; domain memory is proposed in one review card a week; skills change only by the owner's approval, versioned; prompt, model, tools, permissions and trust stage are always the owner's; nothing learned from a tainted sortie becomes a skill without review; a change to skills or prompt is versioned and re-runs the pilot's evaluations, and a drop moves it back a stage. **Inside a pilot** planning, doing and checking stay one loop; promotion through the golden sortie evaluations. |

### F-046

**Misato checks what already exists before adding: same thing, a change, or new**

Today the store drops only exact copies (B-003 for reminders, `factKey` for facts); a reminder with the same title at another time becomes a second one, and a fact that contradicts an earlier one ("I like tea" after "I don't like tea") is added next to it. Misato has no tool to change a reminder. |

| **Check** | Before proposing reminders.add or memory.remember, Misato is shown the existing items that match (same or similar title, the same subject); the same item is not proposed again and the reply says it already exists (with its time or text); a changed one becomes a proposal to change it (reminders.update for title or time; for a fact, the edit of the existing fact, shown old → new on the card), approved like any change; a really new item is added as today; the reply says which of the three it was and why; works in English and Italian; tests cover same, changed and new for reminders and facts, through the scheduler. Calendar and notes follow the same rule when they exist. |

**Backup and restore: agreed loss bounds, off-host snapshots and a restore drill**

| **Issue** | Preserved proposal 1 of the [architecture reassessment](audits/2026-11-06-architecture-reassessment.md#1-backups-and-recovery-highest-reliability-value): reminders, memory, ledger, enrollment and grant state live in one SQLite database per base; losing the disk loses them. Litestream was dropped with Terminal Dogma, and the recovery outcome was dropped with it. No backup exists. |
| **Reproduce** | Remove `~/.nerv` on a disposable base: nothing restores reminders, memory, identity or revoked grants. |
| **Check** | Owner-agreed loss window and restore time; consistent live snapshots (SQLite backup API) on a schedule; retained, encrypted off-host copies with keys kept apart from routine runtime authority; a restore drill onto another location within the agreed bounds that keeps identities, revoked grants and notification checkpoints and replays no old work; no secrets in logs. |

<details>
<summary>Next action, estimates and evidence</summary>

**Next action / closure evidence:** Proposed 2026-11-06 from the reassessment; not accepted scope until the owner sets the bounds. Recommendation: a scheduled snapshot first (simpler, likely enough for personal use); continuous replication such as Litestream only if the agreed loss window is smaller, since it adds storage credentials, monitoring and a dependency, and replication alone copies a damaging deletion. Retention and a tested restore matter more than the tool. Related F-002 (core hardening). P1 because it is data integrity.

**Estimates:** Medium remaining effort for a bounded snapshot/restore path; higher for unattended replication and key recovery. Set 2026-11-06.
